overview_description.description:
Lahza turns the cameras a factory already has into a live monitoring agent.

Most plants only find out about a problem after it costs them something. A near miss that nobody reported. A hygiene breach that surfaces in an audit. A line that sat idle for forty minutes on the night shift. The footage exists, but nobody was watching at the moment it mattered.

With Lahza, your team writes in plain language what to watch for, in English or Arabic, and the system watches the live feed and alerts the moment it happens, with a short documented clip. No CCTV replacement, no re-cabling, no long integration project. It runs on your existing IP cameras and goes live in a day.

Three areas of focus:

Safety. Missing PPE, people in danger zones, unsafe proximity to machines.

Quality and hygiene. Missing hairnets or gloves, clean-zone breaches, missing caps or labels.

Operations. Stopped lines, slow stations, empty workstations, and where the time actually goes.

All video is processed locally on an edge device installed at your site. Nothing is streamed off your premises, and your footage and data stay yours.

Lahza is an AI vision platform based in Amman, built with Jordanian-German engineering and research partnerships with the German Jordanian University and Al Hussein Technical University.

Manufacturing teams use Lahza to see what is really happening on the line, understand what is holding performance back, and improve with confidence, not assumptions.
